gist: Cricket Australia created an independent forum for players and staff involved in the 2018 sandpapergate scandal.
The move follows claims in Usman Khawaja's memoir that the entire team knew about ball tampering.
Chief executive Todd Greenberg stated the confidential forum is not an investigation and involves no penalties.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cricket Australia launched an independent forum for players and staff tied to the 2018 sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events. This follows Usman Khawaja's memoir claiming the entire team knew about the plot, sparking conflicting accounts and a bitter split among players.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The scandal has resurfaced national shame and renewed scrutiny of Cricket Australia's initial investigation, with some players alleging they were not interviewed and David Warner accusing the governing body of a cover-up. Todd Greenberg noted the game is hurting and needs to heal.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Participants can share experiences in a confidential place without judgement or sanction. The Cricket Australia board will decide what information to make public, while officials aim to help the current team focus on performing.

fivew: Cricket Australia, chief executive Todd Greenberg, and current and former players.
Cricket Australia set up an independent forum for individuals involved in the 2018 ball tampering scandal.
Following the release of Usman Khawaja's memoir and announced on a Friday.
To allow participants to share their versions of events and help the sport heal from conflicting accounts.

quotes.text: The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone,
We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal.
